title: First Aid Awareness
blurb: The basics everyone should know in an emergency, who to get, and how to record any first aid given.
siteNotes: Where each first aid kit is kept
Who the first aiders are on each shift
Where and how incidents and first aid are recorded
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-35 (the venue's 10-minute trainer). Taught as written.

CHECK: for choking the trainer says encourage coughing, then back blows and abdominal thrusts if trained. Current first aid guidance is back blows first, then abdominal thrusts; confirm with your first aid provider.

CHECK: burn cooling, firm direct pressure for heavy bleeding, and 999 plus CPR for someone unresponsive and not breathing normally match current NHS and Resuscitation Council advice, but please confirm with your first aid trainer.
Recording first aid: accident book, see the first-aid-accidents session.

cards.title: First Aid Awareness
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- know what to find out before an emergency
- follow the priority order in a serious emergency
- act on the basics and record what happens

cards.title: You do not need to be a first aider
cards.body: You do not have to be a trained first aider to be useful in an emergency. Everyone should know the basics of what to do and, crucially, who to get. Learn these before anything happens, so you are not scrambling when seconds count.

cards.title: Priority order
cards.body: In a serious emergency the order is simple. Do not move a seriously injured person unless leaving them puts them in greater danger, like a fire. Reassure them, keep them still and warm, and stay with them until help arrives.

items.title: Keep yourself safe
items.text: You cannot help if you are hurt too.

cards.title: Four things worth knowing
cards.body: A few basics are worth knowing.

items.title: Burn
items.text: Cool it under cool running water.

items.title: Heavy bleeding
items.text: Apply firm, direct pressure to the wound.

items.title: Choking
items.text: Encourage them to cough. If that fails and you are trained, back blows and abdominal thrusts.

items.title: Not breathing normally
items.text: Unresponsive: call 999, and CPR if trained.

cards.title: Record it, stay in your lane
cards.body: Every incident and any first aid given must be recorded and reported. It is part of looking after people and spotting patterns. First aiders should only work within their training. Everyone else should focus on getting help quickly and keeping the casualty calm.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Know where the kit is and who the first aiders are
- Keep yourself safe, then call 999, then tell the Duty Manager
- Do not move a seriously injured person unless they are in greater danger
- Record and report every incident and any first aid given
- Work within your training

cards.q: In a serious emergency, after keeping yourself safe you should…
options: Wait to see if it gets worse
cards.why: The order is keep yourself safe, call 999, then tell the Duty Manager.

cards.q: Which two things should you know BEFORE an emergency happens?
options: Where the kit is and who the first aiders are
Where the nearest hospital is and who called the ambulance
How much first aid supplies cost and who orders them
Which guest is a doctor and where the stairs are
cards.why: Knowing where the first aid kit is and who your first aiders are means you will not be scrambling when seconds count.

cards.q: You should move a seriously injured person straight away, whatever the situation.
cards.why: Do not move a seriously injured person unless leaving them puts them in greater danger, such as in a fire.

cards.q: For heavy bleeding you should apply…
options: Nothing until a first aider arrives
cards.why: Apply firm, direct pressure to the wound.

cards.q: For a burn you should cool it under cool running water.
cards.why: Cool running water is the first step for a burn.

cards.q: What is the first thing to encourage someone who is choking to do?
cards.why: Encourage them to cough. Only if that fails, and you are trained, give back blows and abdominal thrusts.

cards.q: Any first aid given should be recorded and reported.
cards.why: Every incident and any first aid given must be recorded and reported, which helps spot patterns.

options: Wait for the Duty Manager to say yes
Never help in front of guests
cards.why: First aiders should only work within their training.

cards.q: Someone unresponsive and not breathing normally is a 999 call.
cards.why: If someone is unresponsive and not breathing normally, call 999, and start CPR if you are trained.

cards.q: If you are not a first aider, what is the most useful thing you can do?
options: Do what you have seen on television
Stay out of the way until it is over
Get help quickly and keep the casualty calm
cards.why: Everyone else should focus on getting help quickly, by calling 999 or fetching a first aider, and keeping the casualty calm.
